clue.text: Pain from running, which may be running?

definitions.meaning: a sharp ache in the side brought on by exercise
a running ... is a simple sewing ..., so a ... may itself be running

explanation.surface: A runner wonders whether the ache in their side is still going.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a side cramp felt by joggers and a loop of thread in sewing, one kind of which is called running.

clue.text: Grey makes lin chased for a penny — that's flattering!

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Grey makes lin chased for a penny — that's flattering!', mixes 27-down's clue with this one; the same text is shown on two lights.

clue.text: Where batsman stands to gain

definitions.meaning: in cricket the batsman stands in the crease, the line marked at the wicket
a rise or growth in amount

explanation.surface: A cricketer's position at the wicket is said to bring profit.
explanation.walkthrough: The crease is the white line in front of the stumps where a cricket batsman takes guard.
explanation.definitionFit: A rise in number or size is a gain, a common synonym.

clue.text: Report followed, being immaculate

indicators.note: report means a word spoken out, so we want one sounding like a word for followed

parts.note: chased means followed in pursuit

explanation.surface: A news report says someone was tailed while remaining spotless.
explanation.definitionFit: Pure and without sexual sin, so unblemished in morals.

clue.text: Christmas activity which is slow initially, then mad!

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of the word slow

parts.note: hopping mad means furious, so hopping can stand for mad

explanation.surface: Seasonal present-buying starts at a crawl and ends in frenzy.
explanation.walkthrough: HOPPING alone means mad only through the idiom 'hopping mad'.
explanation.definitionFit: Buying presents in crowded stores is a typical seasonal pastime before the holiday.

clue.text: Ring bear up

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the bear's name is read from the bottom

parts.note: Pooh is the famous storybook bear, Winnie-the-Pooh

explanation.surface: Someone is told to tolerate a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bear' looks like a verb, tolerate, but is the noun: the bear Pooh.
explanation.definitionFit: A circular band, as of metal or wood, is a type of ring.

clue.text: It's cheap abstract art GI that's eclectic

indicators.note: abstract suggests the letters are pulled out of shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: Cheap abstract work is dismissed as a magpie mix of styles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abstract' reads as an art style but signals that ITS and CHEAP are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A work imitating or mixing other styles borrows from many sources, which is what eclectic means.

clue.text: Crooked man held by it for life ultimately, a prisoner

indicators.note: held by says the scrambled word sits inside the word it
crooked suggests the letters of man are bent out of order
ultimately asks for the final letter of life

explanation.surface: A bent man is locked up for life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crooked' gives NMA, which 'held by' places inside IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone confined in a jail is one of its occupants.

clue.text: Something slippery in the SIEIRIBII country spoken of

indicators.note: spoken of means the name of the country is said out loud

parts.note: Greece is a country in southern Europe

explanation.surface: Something slippery is found in the land being discussed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'SIEIRIBII' is stray print in the clue as held.
explanation.definitionFit: Oily lubricant makes surfaces slick, so it is a slippery substance.

clue.text: Treatment for investigators held in bird, con having fled

indicators.note: held in says the investigators sit inside the shortened bird
having fled says the word con goes away from the bird's name

parts.note: a falcon is a bird of prey
taken as written
the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency, a body of investigators

explanation.surface: Agents are caught inside a bird after a swindler escapes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having fled' removes CON from FALCON, leaving FAL, and 'held in' puts CIA inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A beauty treatment for the face given at a salon is a well-known example.

clue.text: Against battle, it's clear

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
the Somme was a First World War battle in northern France

explanation.surface: Someone opposed to a famous battle declares the matter settled.
explanation.definitionFit: A clear is a menu term for a thin transparent soup, which is what this dish is.

clue.text: Stand up crookedly and sweep in to it

indicators.note: crookedly suggests the letters of stand up are set askew

explanation.surface: Someone stands awkwardly and sweeps.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: the thing you sweep dirt into.
explanation.definitionFit: The flat scoop held at floor level receives what the brush gathers.

clue.text: Move fingers playfully around muscle that's multi-coloured

indicators.note: around says the guitar-playing word wraps about the muscle

parts.note: to strum is to run the fingers loosely over guitar strings
pec is short for pectoral, a chest muscle

explanation.surface: A guitarist plays idly over a muscle that shows many colours.
explanation.definitionFit: A band of colours such as a rainbow is the standard example of this, so it is something multi-coloured.

clue.text: One in Panama, perhaps, for American break

indicators.note: in places the numeral for one inside the headwear

parts.note: a Panama is a type of straw hat, the perhaps marking an example
I is the Roman numeral for one
US is short for American, United States

explanation.surface: Someone in Panama takes an American holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Panama, perhaps' looks like the country but is the straw hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A pause or gap in continuity is a synonym of a break.

clue.text: Leave shy little bird

parts.note: go means leave
to shy is to throw, as is to sling

explanation.surface: A bashful small bird is told to go away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shy' looks like timid but is the verb meaning throw, as at a coconut shy.
explanation.definitionFit: A young goose is a small chick, so a little bird.

clue.text: Primate set about small church area

indicators.note: set about says the primate is placed around the small letter

parts.note: an ape is a primate
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: A monkey goes round a little part of a chapel.
explanation.definitionFit: The recess at the east end of a church, often semicircular, is a specific part of the building.

clue.text: Wasting of a prize

parts.note: a trophy is a prize such as a cup

explanation.surface: Someone frets about squandering a trophy.
explanation.definitionFit: Medical term for the shrinking or withering of muscle or tissue, which is a wasting away.

clue.text: Dynasty to rule endlessly, the result of excess

parts.note: the Han dynasty ruled ancient China

indicators.note: endlessly removes the final letter of the word for rule

parts.note: to govern is to rule

explanation.surface: A royal line seeks to rule forever and pays for overindulgence.
explanation.definitionFit: The headache and nausea after too much alcohol follow drinking to excess.

clue.text: It's played from the autumn, involving kicker heading to back

indicators.note: involving says the season wraps around the shifted kicker

parts.note: fall is the American word for autumn

indicators.note: heading to back moves the first letter of the kicker's word to its end

parts.note: a boot is what kicks a ball

explanation.surface: A game played from autumn involves a kicker heading backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading to back' moves B of BOOT to the end, giving OOTB, which 'involving' puts inside FALL.
explanation.definitionFit: A team sport in which players kick a ball, so a game that is played.

clue.text: Hold plate of cereal?

parts.note: bran is a breakfast cereal
a dish is a plate

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to hold a bowl of breakfast cereal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plate of cereal' gives DISH of BRAN, written in the order BRAN DISH.
explanation.definitionFit: To wave a weapon about menacingly is to hold it up for show.

clue.text: Very seriously overweight friend

parts.note: fat means overweight
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: A friend is described as dangerously heavy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being hurt or wounded in a deadly way is about as serious as an injury gets.

clue.text: Leonine exclamation at the state of its meat sounded

indicators.note: sounded means the word for the meat's condition is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a lion eats its meat raw, uncooked

explanation.surface: A lion cries out at the condition of its dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: The homophone works in a non-rhotic British accent, where the final R is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: The loud deep cry of a lion is its best-known noise.

clue.text: Opposition hoodwinked riches during broadcast

indicators.note: during says the word for hoodwinked sits within the word for broadcast

parts.note: to sow is to broadcast seed by scattering
had means hoodwinked, as in 'you've been had'

explanation.surface: The opposition tricked people during a broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: In British politics the Shadow cabinet is the opposition's front bench. 'riches' is stray print from 31-across.
explanation.definitionFit: The main opposition party's team of spokespeople in Britain is named after a dark outline that follows the government.

clue.text: Pole needed by athlete, cheerful person

parts.note: S stands for south, one of the poles
a miler is a runner who races over a mile

explanation.surface: A pole vault is needed by a cheerful athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who grins a lot is a happy, cheery person.

clue.text: Waste the card in view

indicators.note: in places the joker inside the word for view

parts.note: to see is to view
a card is a joker, and so is a wag

explanation.surface: Someone discards the card that is showing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'card' is not a playing card but an old word for a comic person, a wag.
explanation.definitionFit: Effluent carried away by drains is waste matter.

clue.text: Deference in collecting the silver

indicators.note: collecting says the word for in wraps around the metal symbol

parts.note: at home means in, as in staying in
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Respect is shown by gathering up the silverware.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word but supplies HOME, as in 'staying in' or 'at home'.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying tribute or respect to someone is an act of deference.

clue.text: Food store given a light arrival of goods

parts.note: a deli is a shop selling prepared foods
a Very light is a coloured signal flare

explanation.surface: A grocery is lit up when stock comes in.
explanation.walkthrough: A Very light is a flare fired from a pistol, named after its American inventor.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods being handed over or brought to a customer is what a drop-off of a parcel amounts to.

clue.text: Terribly bored after fight, heading to bac ing for clothes space

indicators.note: after puts the scrambled word behind the fight

parts.note: war is a fight between nations

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters of bored are badly scrambled

explanation.surface: Bored after a fight, someone looks for a place to hang clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terribly' rearranges BORED to DROBE, placed after WAR. The words 'heading to bac ing' are stray print from 18-down.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall cupboard for hanging garments is a storage space for clothes.

clue.text: Breaking the law brings

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Breaking the law brings', is cut short: the definition word (riches) has strayed into 22-down.
